newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan frees detained Japanese fishing boat.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan frees detained Japanese fishing boat.

text.p: Taiwan repatriated a Japanese fishing boat on Tuesday, five days after seizing it for violating the island's territorial waters, state media said.
The vessel with 11 crew was allowed to leave Taiwan after its Japanese owner paid T$150,000 (US$5,400) in fines for a breach of Taiwan's fishing law, state television said.
The Japanese tuna boat was detained on Thursday off Taiwan's southern county of Pingtung and charged with penetrating the island's 12 nautical-mile territorial waters.
All of its harvest and fishing equipment were confiscated.
It was the first time that Taiwan had detained a Japanese vessel since the 1980s, local media reported.

The incident was the most serious involving Taiwan and Japan since a sovereignty dispute in 1996 arising from rival claims to a chain of small uninhabited East China Sea isles known to Japan as the Senkakus and to Taiwan and China as the Diaoyus.
Taiwan has no diplomatic ties with Japan, which recognises only Beijing's communist government.
Taiwan and China have been rivals since a civil war split them in 1949.
